title: No requirement gives the user a view of one order and its lines
why: Brief: 'add, edit, and remove order lines' and 'order lines belonging to each order'. R-09 stops at a list ('shows number, customer name, date and total') and R-03 shows only 'the customer's orders with their totals'. R-11, R-12 and R-13 act on lines, but nothing says where the lines are shown, how an order is opened, or that a line total or the notes are ever displayed. R-14 computes a line total that no criterion shows. Walking the flow customer > create order > add lines > see total, the step after R-06 has no requirement, so the tester has nothing to test it against. R-07 notes can be edited but never read.
suggested:
### R-28 [MUST] View an order
- Creating an order opens it; the order list and the customer detail each open an order when the user selects it.
- The order view shows the number, customer name, date, notes, every line with description, quantity, unit price and line total in the order they were added (A-08), and the order total.
- From the order view the user can edit the order (R-07), add, edit and remove lines (R-11 to R-13) and delete the order (R-08).
- The user can reach the customer list and the order list from every screen.

title: Unreadable stored data leaves the user in a state with no way out
why: R-20: 'the app shows an error and does not write over it'. No criterion says what the user can do next. Export is LATER (R-25), so the data cannot be taken out, and starting again would need the browser's developer tools. Every main flow stays closed for good, or, if the lists render empty, the first save writes over the data R-20 protects. Brief: 'useful empty or error states'. This is a dead end under checklist item 2.
suggested:
### R-20 [MUST] Unreadable stored data is not overwritten
- If the saved data cannot be read, or was saved by a newer version of the app, the app shows an error instead of the lists; nothing can be added or changed, so nothing is written over the data.
- The error says what happened and offers two ways out: copy the stored text, or start with empty data.
- Starting with empty data needs a confirmation that says the old data will be lost; only then is the stored data replaced.

title: No way to leave a form without saving
why: R-17: 'nothing is saved until all fields are valid'. No requirement offers Cancel, so a user who opened a form by mistake, or cannot satisfy a rule, has no stated way out. R-02 says of an invalid edit that 'the old values stay', but R-07 and R-12 say nothing of the kind.
suggested:
Add to R-17:
- Every form has a Cancel action that closes it and discards what was typed; the saved values stay as they were.
- An invalid edit of an order or a line is not saved and the old values stay, as in R-02.

title: Delete customer: confirm first or refuse first, and no pointer to the way out
why: R-04 has 'The user must confirm before a customer is deleted' and 'A customer who has orders cannot be deleted; the app says why and how many orders block it'. It reads two ways: confirm and then be refused, or be refused at once. The message also does not say how to proceed, though R-18 holds empty states to saying 'what to do next'. The rule itself was decided (Q-01) and is not reopened here.
suggested:
Replace the R-04 criteria with:
- If the customer has no orders, the user must confirm before the customer is deleted.
- If the customer has orders, the app asks for no confirmation; it says the customer cannot be deleted, how many orders block it, and that those orders must be deleted first. No data changes.

title: With export LATER, the only copy of the data is one browser profile
why: Implied line: 'data must survive a reload and must never be lost silently'. A-01: 'Data stays on the device'. A-09: 'Deleting is permanent'. R-25 is LATER, so clearing site data or changing browser removes everything with no warning and no backup. It does not block first use, so LATER can stand, but the user should be told. What settles it: the human either keeps R-25 LATER with the assumption below or moves R-25 to MUST.
suggested: - **A-11** The data lives only in this browser on this device. Clearing the browser's site data removes it and there is no backup until R-25 exists. The customer list shows a one-line note saying so.

title: R-10 asks for both filter and search where the brief says one or the other
why: Brief: 'Keep the scope light' and 'search or filter customers and orders'. R-10 requires both: 'filtered by one customer and searched by order number or customer name'. Customer orders are already visible in the customer detail (R-03), so the filter is not needed for first use. What settles it: the human says whether both mechanisms are wanted in the first version.
suggested:
### R-10 [MUST] Search orders
- Typing in the search box shows only orders whose number or customer name contains the text, case-insensitive, ignoring leading and trailing spaces.
- An empty search shows all orders.

### R-29 [LATER] Filter orders by one customer

title: R-14 is worded around how the amount is computed
why: R-14: 'computed in whole cents with no rounding error'. Whole cents is an implementation choice already in A-04. The user can only observe the amount, so the example is the real criterion.
suggested: - A line total is quantity × unit price and is exact to the cent (for example 3 × 0.10 shows 0.30, and 3 × 19.99 shows 59.97).

title: R-16 names an API instead of what the user sees
why: R-16: 'formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat`'. A user cannot observe that, while they can observe the separators and the euro sign. A-04 already says the format follows the browser's locale.
suggested: - Every amount is shown with two decimals and the euro sign, with separators that follow the browser's language (for example 1,234.50 in English and 1.234,50 in Romanian).

title: Second criterion of R-19 is a storage design, not something a user sees
why: R-19: 'All data is stored under one `localStorage` key as JSON with a schema version'. No user can observe this, and the data model sketch already states it. The first criterion alone is the user-visible requirement.
suggested: Delete the second criterion of R-19; the one-key format stays in the Data model sketch.

title: R-22 leaves phone, address and the search text out of its list
why: R-22 names 'Any name, email, description or note'. A-02 makes phone and address 'free text' too, and search text may be echoed back in a no-results message (R-18). ADR-002 states the rule without exceptions: 'user text is never rendered as HTML'. A tester working from the list would miss two fields.
suggested: - Any text the user typed, in any field or search box, containing HTML such as `<b>x</b>` is displayed literally, never interpreted.

title: Empty states miss the customer with no orders and order creation with no customers
why: R-18 lists 'No customers, no orders, an order with no lines and a search with no results'. Three states fall outside it. A customer detail with no orders (R-03) is one. Creating an order when no customer exists is another: R-06 says only 'An order can only be created for an existing customer', and on an empty order list the next step is to add a customer, not an order. The third is a customer filter with no match (R-10), which is not a search. Brief: 'useful empty or error states'.
suggested:
Add to R-18:
- A customer with no orders shows a message offering to create the first order for that customer.
- With no customers yet, the order list says a customer must be added first and links to the customer form; an order cannot be started.
- A filter or search on orders with no match says so and offers to clear it.

title: No rule for the order date or the notes
why: R-06: 'the date of today, which the user can change'. R-07 lets the user change date and notes. R-17 needs a message 'naming the rule it broke', but neither field has a rule: a cleared date, an impossible date or very long notes are all undefined, and R-09 sorts by that date. R-06 also does not say whether notes can be entered at creation, though the data model has them. Brief: 'basic validation'.
suggested:
Add to R-06:
- The date is required and must be a real calendar date; past and future dates are allowed.
- The form also accepts optional notes, up to 500 characters after trimming; the same rules apply in R-07.

title: What the user may type as a price is not defined
why: R-11: 'a unit price from 0.00 to 1 000 000.00 with at most two decimals'. A-04: 'display formatting uses the browser's locale'. A user on a comma locale sees 12,50 € and may type 12,50, or type 1,000.50 in English. The requirement reads two ways: rejected, or accepted as a different amount. A wrongly read amount would change totals with no warning. R-12 also does not say how the current price appears in the edit field.
suggested:
Add to R-11:
- The unit price accepts a dot or a comma as the decimal separator and no thousands separators; anything else shows an error next to the field.
- When a line is edited, the unit price field shows the saved price with two decimals.

title: Removing a line has no confirmation while deleting anything else does
why: R-04 and R-08 require confirmation. R-13 says only 'Removing a line takes it out of the order', and A-09 says 'Deleting is permanent; there is no undo or trash'. One misclick loses a line for good. It may be a deliberate choice for speed, but nothing says so. What settles it: the human chooses to confirm, or records that no confirmation is intended.
suggested:
### R-13 [MUST] Remove an order line
- After confirmation the line is taken out of the order and the order total updates at once.

title: After a failed save, what happens to what the user typed is not stated
why: R-21: 'the app shows an error and the change is not shown as saved'. This can be met by closing the form and dropping the input, while AGENTS.md rule 6 says 'never lose user data silently'. With a full quota the user also has no stated next step.
suggested:
Add to R-21:
- The form stays open with what the user typed, so the save can be retried; the error says the browser's storage is full or unavailable and that deleting data frees space.

title: Two tabs of the app may lose changes or repeat an order number
why: A-01 says 'One user, one browser' but says nothing about two tabs, which one user can easily open. If each tab holds its own copy, the later save overwrites the earlier one. Implied line: 'must never be lost silently'. R-06: 'Order numbers are unique and never reused'. What settles it: the human says whether two tabs are in scope; the outcome also depends on the design, which does not exist yet.
suggested:
Add to R-19:
- With the app open in two tabs, a change saved in one tab is not lost when the other tab saves, and order numbers stay unique.
Or, if out of scope, extend A-01: Only one tab is open at a time; two tabs are not supported.

title: Nothing says whether two customers can have the same name
why: R-01 sets only a length for the name. Two customers called the same would look identical in the R-10 customer filter and could be confused when creating an order (R-06), which A-06 makes costly because 'An order's customer cannot be changed'. What settles it: the human says whether duplicates are allowed.
suggested: - **A-12** Two customers may have the same name or email; wherever a customer is picked, the email is shown next to the name.

title: R-01 omits phone and address, and the 200-character limit is in no criterion
why: R-01: 'saves a name (1 to 100 characters after trimming) and an optional email'. A-02 lists 'email, phone, address (all optional, free text up to 200 characters)', and R-02 edits phone and address 'The same rules as R-01'. R-01 has no rule for them, so the create form may lack two fields the edit form has, and a 300-character address has no defined result.
suggested:
Replace the first criterion of R-01 with:
- Given the customer form, when the user saves a name (1 to 100 characters after trimming) and optionally an email, phone and address (each up to 200 characters), then the customer appears in the list.

title: R-10 lacks the search details R-05 spells out
why: R-05 says 'ignoring leading and trailing spaces' and 'An empty search shows all customers'. R-10 says only 'case-insensitive; both apply together'. The two searches may behave differently, and neither an empty search nor clearing the filter is defined. If PO-6 is accepted, its text covers this and only the search part applies.
suggested:
Add to R-10:
- Search ignores leading and trailing spaces; an empty search and no chosen customer show all orders.

title: Export of personal data is deferred to LATER, so the app cannot export a person's data
why: R-25 reads '[LATER] Export and import of the data as JSON', and no MUST produces a file. R-03 only shows fields on screen. LD-08 requires 'An export for the person is structured, commonly used and machine-readable' and says 'a PDF, a screenshot or a printed table is not machine-readable, a JSON or CSV file is'. Article 20(1) is the source. R-25 also describes the whole data set, which would hand one person the data of every other customer, so moving it to MUST is not enough. The app as specified holds personal data it cannot export.
suggested:
### R-28 [MUST] Export one customer's data
- From the customer detail, the user can download a JSON file holding that customer's fields and all their orders with their lines.
- The file holds no data of any other customer.

### R-25 [LATER] Import of the data, and export of the whole data set, as JSON

title: Access needs more than the data: purpose and retention are not part of what the person gets
why: R-03 reads 'The customer detail shows all fields and the customer's orders with their totals', which is a screen, not a copy. LD-06 says the right of access needs a path in the app: 'which data is held, for what purpose, how long', with 'the copy ... provided in a commonly used electronic form, within one month of the request'. The file itself is LEG-1. This item adds the purpose and the retention to it.
suggested:
Add to R-28:
- The file also states the purpose of the data (A-11) and how long it is kept (A-12), so the user can answer a person's access request with this one file.

title: The refusal to delete a customer rests on no listed exception and does not say how to erase
why: R-04 reads 'A customer who has orders cannot be deleted; the app says why and how many orders block it, and no data changes.' LD-07 reads 'a refusal rests on a listed exception and the app says which'. Having orders is neither of the exceptions the rule names: 17(3)(b) legal obligation or 17(3)(e) legal claim. A-10 rules out issued invoices, so no stored invoice blocks erasure either. It is advisory because a route exists: R-08 deletes the orders, then R-04 deletes the customer. Nothing in the app tells the user that route. The human chose this rule for R-04, so the suggestion keeps it and only adds the way out.
suggested:
Replace the second criterion of R-04:
- A customer who has orders is not deleted while those orders exist; the app says how many orders block it, that no legal retention applies, and that deleting those orders (R-08) and then the customer erases all of this customer's data. No data changes at this step.

title: No personal data field has a stated purpose
why: The data model lists Customer 'name string, email string, phone string, address string' and Order 'notes string', and A-02 defines them. No requirement or assumption says what each is for. LD-02 reads 'Every personal data field has a stated purpose and is used only for it' and 'a field with no purpose has no legal ground to exist'. Under LD-01 these fields are personal data, as is 'a customer number joined to a name', which covers Customer.id and Order.customerId. Order.notes and OrderLine.description are free text and can also hold personal data.
suggested: - **A-11** Purpose of personal data: `name`, `email`, `phone` and `address` identify and contact the customer an order belongs to; `id` and `customerId` link orders to that customer; `notes` and line `description` record what the order is about and should not hold details about other people. The data is used for nothing else.

title: Fields that no requirement needs: createdAt, and phone and address as far as the flows go
why: The data model has 'createdAt ISO string' on Customer and on Order. No requirement reads either: R-03 does not show it and R-09 sorts by 'newest date first, then highest number first'. On Customer it is a fact about an identifiable person. Phone and address appear only as edit and display fields (R-02, R-03), and R-01 names only 'a name ... and an optional email'. No flow uses them. LD-03 reads 'The app stores only the personal data its purpose needs, by default' and warns against 'a field "because it may be useful later"'.
suggested:
In the data model sketch, remove `createdAt` from Customer and Order unless a requirement uses it.
Change A-02: **A-02** Customer fields: name (required), email, phone, address (all optional, free text up to 200 characters, empty by default). Keep phone and address only if the human confirms the purpose in A-11; otherwise remove them.

title: No retention rule for Customer or Order
why: A-09 reads 'Deleting is permanent; there is no undo or trash', and that is the only thing said about how data ends. The Customer and Order entities have no end date. LD-05 reads 'every entity with personal data has a retention rule' and 'a customer record with no end date is kept forever by default'. No domain skill exists in the project to carry it, and the period is a human decision.
suggested: - **A-12** Retention: a customer and their orders are kept until the user deletes them, and no later than NEEDS HUMAN: the period after the customer's last order. The app deletes nothing by itself; the user applies this rule with R-04 and R-08. No legal retention applies while the app issues no invoices (A-10).

title: The data model does not name its personal data categories, purposes and retention
why: The 'Data model sketch' lists fields only. LD-10 reads 'The categories of personal data, their purposes and their retention are written down' and 'the requirements and the data model are that somewhere, and a reviewer can check them'. Purposes and retention are LEG-4 and LEG-6. This item puts the record where a reviewer looks for it.
suggested:
Add under the data model sketch:
Personal data: Customer `id`, `name`, `email`, `phone`, `address`; Order `customerId`, `notes`; OrderLine `description` when it names a person. Purpose: A-11. Retention: A-12.

title: No requirement keeps personal data out of error text, URLs and the page title
why: LD-09 reads 'Personal data does not leak into logs, error messages, URLs or the storage of a shared machine'. AGENTS.md rule 6 bans `console.log` under `src/`, which covers logs. Nothing covers the rest. R-10 adds a search by customer name and R-03 a customer detail, and neither says what the address or the title carries. R-17, R-20 and R-21 add error text. No requirement line breaks the rule today. What settles it is this criterion, or the URL scheme in docs/UI-SPEC.md, which does not exist yet.
suggested:
### R-29 [MUST] Personal data stays out of errors, URLs and titles
- Error messages, the page title and the URL never contain a customer's name, email, phone or address, or the text typed into a search; a page is addressed by `id` only.

title: Personal data sits in plain localStorage, and the requirements do not say the machine is private
why: R-19 reads 'All data is stored under one localStorage key as JSON', and the brief mandates localStorage, so the storage itself is a given. LD-09 names 'data left in localStorage on a shared computer' as a disclosure. A-01 reads 'One user, one browser, no accounts', which says one user but not that the machine is theirs. There is no lock and no way to clear everything. R-20 keeps unreadable data and refuses to write over it, so in that state the app offers no way to erase it. ADR-002 sends delivery to GitHub Pages, where a project site shares its origin, and so its localStorage, with the owner's other sites under the same github.io name. To settle it: the human states whether the app may run on a shared machine, and the devops decision names the origin.
suggested:
Change A-01: **A-01** One user, one browser, no accounts, on a device only that user can open. Data stays on the device; nothing is sent anywhere.

### R-30 [MUST] Erase all data on this device
- After a confirmation that says all customers and orders will be gone for good, the user can remove the app's stored data, also when the stored data is unreadable (R-20).

title: The project has no LICENSE file and no decision on its licence
why: The repository root holds no LICENSE file, and AGENTS.md does not list one in its structure. LL-11 reads 'The project has a LICENSE file' and 'without a LICENSE file the project itself is all rights reserved (LL-02), so nobody, not even a colleague, may legally use it'. AGENTS.md cites docs/decisions/ADR-001-stack.md, but that file does not exist yet, so the skill's question whether ADR-001 says what the licence is has no answer. No third-party library, font or icon set is named: AGENTS.md says 'no dependencies'. So LL-01 to LL-10 have nothing to bite on until docs/UI-SPEC.md exists.
suggested: - **A-13** The project ships a `LICENSE` file at the root, and its licence is named by SPDX identifier in ADR-001 (NEEDS HUMAN: the licence). Any library, font, icon set or adapted design added later is named with its SPDX identifier in a decision first.

title: The LATER invoice line carries obligations the current model and flows would not meet
why: A-10 puts legal invoices out of scope, so LE-01 to LE-08 break nothing today. R-23 is a heading with no criteria, though, and the choices made now would collide with it later. The data model has no supplier, VAT number, tax or supply date, while LE-01 says 'A data model that cannot hold one of them cannot issue a lawful invoice'. R-07, R-12 and R-08 edit and delete orders, while the LE-03 review asks whether lines can be 'changed through the order'. R-04 and A-09 delete freely, while LE-07 reads 'Retention beats erasure'. To settle it: the human confirms that the app's output is never used as an invoice, or adds these criteria when R-23 is taken up.
suggested:
### R-23 [LATER] Issue invoices (numbered, immutable, printable or PDF)
- Before this is built: the data model holds every Article 226 detail, the numbering is sequential and unique, an issued invoice is read-only and independent of later order edits, a correction is a new document, the retention period is named in a decision, erasure respects it, and the customer's acceptance of electronic invoices is recorded.
